extracted.intended_audience: patent agents, trade mark/design practitioners, solicitors, and applicants (inventors/owners) dealing with UK patent/design/trade mark office procedure under the 1883 Act
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and administrative standards for handling registers, certified copies, corrections, alterations, prosecutions, and international priority under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act (1883). Covers comptroller powers, court rectification, certificates, postal filing rules, and related offences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to copies of register entries on payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any entry in such register shall be given to any person requiring the same on payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are prescribed by rules (see Patents Rules, Designs Rules, Trade Marks Rules). For designs, a copy can be obtained only when the copyright has expired (sect. 52, sub‑sect. (2), Designs Rules, 33), but a certificate of existence of the copyright may be obtained under sect. 53. Office copy fees and certifying fees referenced in Schedule of Fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of sealed extracts in evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed or written copies or extracts, purporting to be certified by the comptroller and sealed with the seal of the patent office, of or from patents, specifications, disclaimers and other documents in the patent office and of or from registers and other books kept there, shall be admitted in evidence in all Courts ... without further proof or production of the originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is based on earlier statutes (Patent Law Amendment Act 1852 etc.). The certified copy or extract must be sealed with the seal of the Patent Office to have this evidentiary effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of designs/trade marks must state purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of certificates of any entry on the Registers of Designs or Trade Marks the legal proceeding for which the certificate is granted is to be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs Rules, 57 and Trade Marks Rules, 34 require the purpose to be stated. No identical provision exists in the Patent Rules; in patents the purposes for which a certificate is to be used will probably require to be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositing and obtaining certified copies in other jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified and sealed copies of all specifications, drawings, and amendments are deposited in the Edinburgh Museum of Science and Art, the Enrolments Office of the Chancery Division in Ireland, and the Rolls Office in the Isle of Man, and certified copies or extracts can be obtained there and will be admitted as evidence in Scotland, Ireland, and the Isle of Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies printed and sealed shall be transmitted within twenty‑one days after acceptance/allowance. Certified copies there are admitted in evidence without further proof or production of originals (see sect. 100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court power to rectify registers (rectification by court)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may, on the application of any person aggrieved by the omission without sufficient cause of the name of any person from any register kept under this Act, or by any entry made without sufficient cause in any such register, make such order for making, expunging, or varying the entry, as the Court thinks fit; or the Court may refuse the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court may also make orders as to costs, decide questions necessary or expedient for rectification, direct issues to be tried for questions of fact, and may award damages to the party aggrieved. Any order rectifying a register shall direct that due notice of the rectification be given to the comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical errors by comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may, on request in writing accompanied by the prescribed fee, correct any clerical error in or in connexion with an application for a patent, or for registration of a design or trade mark; and correct any clerical error in the name, style, or address of the registered proprietor of a patent, design, or trade mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub‑section (c) also enables cancellation of the entry or part of the entry of a trade mark on the register provided the applicant supplies a statutory declaration proving identity (name, address, calling). For forms and fees see the referenced Patents/Designs/Trade Marks Forms and Schedule of Fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: comptroller corrections limited to clerical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub‑sections (a) and (b) are restricted to the correction of clerical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial errors in specifications of letters patent may be corrected only by leave under section 18 (i.e., a different, more formal correction procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for altering a registered trade mark (non‑essential particulars)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registered proprietor of any trade mark may apply to the Court for leave to add to or alter such mark in any particular, not being an essential particular within the meaning of this Act, and the Court may refuse or grant leave on such terms as it may think fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No alteration will be allowed that amounts to an alteration in an 'essential particular' (see sect. 64). Sub‑section (2) requires notice to the comptroller and entitles the comptroller to be heard. If leave is granted, the comptroller will alter the register on proof and payment of the prescribed fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and right to be heard before court applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of any intended application to the Court under the trade mark alteration section shall be given to the comptroller by the applicant; and the comptroller shall be entitled to be heard on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade Marks Rules require forms/notice periods (e.g., fourteen days' notice referenced). The comptroller's involvement is procedural and he must be given an opportunity to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller must give opportunity to be heard before adverse exercise of discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any discretionary power is by this Act given to the comptroller, he shall not exercise that power adversely to the applicant ... without (if so required within the prescribed time by the applicant) giving the applicant an opportunity of being heard personally or by his agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comptroller is required to give ten days' notice before exercising his power adversely to the applicant; within five days from the date when such notice would be delivered the applicant must notify whether he intends to be heard. See Patents Rules, Designs Rules, Trade Marks Rules for precise timing and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's certificate prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate purporting to be under the hand of the comptroller as to any entry, matter, or thing which he is authorised by this Act ... to make or do, shall be prima facie evidence of the entry having been made, and of the contents thereof, and of the matter or thing having been done or left undone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several kinds of certificates exist (e.g., renewal certificates, certificates for registration, certificates for legal proceedings or for foreign filings). The purpose for which the certificate is required should be stated; fee for such certificate is noted in the Rules/Schedule of Fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade marks: certificate requirements and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: In relation to trade marks the comptroller's certificate is of four kinds (for legal proceedings; for applying for registration in foreign countries; of any application made and proceedings thereon; of refusal to register an old mark). The person applying is to state for what purposes he requires the certificate; two unmounted copies of each mark must accompany the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cotton marks and coloured marks the two unmounted copies of the mark must agree in every respect with the representations that formed part of the application for registration (Trade Marks Instructions, 39–41). Forms are in Trade Marks Forms (R, S, T, L etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal filing deemed date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application, notice, or other document authorised or required to be left, made, or given at the patent office or to the comptroller, may be sent by a prepaid letter through the post; and if so sent shall be deemed to have been left, made, or given respectively at the time when the letter containing the same would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In proving such service it is sufficient to prove that the letter was properly addressed and put into the post. By sect. 13, every patent is to be sealed as of the day of application; where application is made by letter, the postal delivery time governs the application date even if never actually received. Applicants should keep exact particulars of posting (address copy, name of person who posted, place posted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded days extension for filings/payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the last day fixed by this Act for leaving documents or paying any fee at the patent office shall fall on Christmas Day, Good Friday, or on a Saturday or Sunday, or any day observed as a Bank holiday or day of public fast or thanksgiving, it shall be lawful to leave such document or to pay such fee on the day next following such excluded day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Office is closed on those days (Patents Rules, 7). Bank holidays include Easter Monday, Whit Monday, first Monday in August, and December 26th as observed days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations by infant or lunatic (substitute acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person is, by reason of infancy, lunacy, or other inability, incapable of making any declaration or doing anything required or permitted by this Act, then the guardian or committee of such incapable person, or if there be none, any person appointed by any Court or judge possessing jurisdiction in respect of the property of incapable persons ... may make such declaration ... and do such thing in the name and on behalf of such incapable person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All acts done by such substitute shall be as effectual as if done by the person for whom he is substituted. The comptroller may, with Board of Trade sanction and upon production of other evidence and subject to terms, dispense with acts, signatures, declarations, or evidence where reasonable cause prevents compliance (see Patents/Designs/Trade Marks Rules references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of accepted specifications to external offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of all specifications, drawings, and amendments left at the patent office after commencement of this Act, printed for and sealed with the seal of the patent office, shall be transmitted to the Edinburgh Museum of Science and Art, the Enrolments Office of the Chancery Division in Ireland, and the Rolls Office in the Isle of Man, within twenty‑one days after they shall respectively have been accepted or allowed at the patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies of or extracts from any such documents shall be given to any person requiring the same on payment of the prescribed fee and shall be admitted in evidence in Scotland and Ireland and in the Isle of Man without further proof or production of the originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Trade power to make general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Trade may from time to time make such general rules and do such things as they think expedient, subject to the provisions of this Act, for regulating the practice of registration, classifying goods for designs and trade marks, making/ requiring duplicates, regulating publishing and selling of copies, making indexes and abridgments, presentation of copies to patentees and public authorities, and generally regulating the business of the patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms in the first schedule may be altered by such rules. Rules made must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and advertised twice in the official journal; either House may resolve within forty days to annul such rules (without prejudice to actions done under them in the meantime). Rules have been issued under this section for patents, designs, and trade marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration/amendment of statutory forms by Board of Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: Any of the forms in the first schedule to this Act may be altered or amended by rules made by the Board of Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alterations by rule are judicially noticed and become of the same effect as if contained in the Act (subject to Parliamentary oversight and annulment procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's annual report duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller shall, before the first day of June in every year, cause a report respecting the execution by or under him of this Act to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, and therein shall include for the year all general rules made and an account of all fees, salaries, allowances, and other money received and paid under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides transparency of practice and rule‑making during the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: International arrangements and priority (foreign filing priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Her Majesty makes any arrangement with any foreign government for mutual protection of inventions, designs, and trade marks, any person who has applied for protection in that foreign state shall be entitled to a patent or registration under this Act in priority to other applicants and such patent/registration shall have the same date as the date of the protection obtained in such foreign state, provided application in the UK is made within seven months for patents and within four months for designs and trade marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the UK or use/exhibition/use of the invention/design/trade mark during those respective periods shall not invalidate the UK patent/registration. However, the proprietor is not entitled to recover damages for infringements happening prior to the date of actual acceptance of the complete specification or actual registration in the UK. The section applies only to foreign states declared by Order in Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formalities under international priority provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for the grant of a patent, or registration of a design or trade mark under the international arrangement section must be made in the same manner as an ordinary application under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In trade marks, any trade mark which has been duly applied for in the country of origin may be registered under this Act. Orders in Council determine which foreign states are covered and for how long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for false representation of patent/design/trade mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who represents that any article sold by him is a patented article when no patent has been granted for the same, or describes any design or trade mark applied to any article sold by him as registered when it is not so, shall be liable for every offence on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding five pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person is deemed to represent an article as patented or registered if he sells the article with words such as 'patent', 'patented', 'registered' or any words expressing or implying that a patent or registration has been obtained, stamped, engraved, impressed on, or otherwise applied to the article. The section likely applies even where a patent/registration has expired; see case law references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for unauthorised use of Royal arms
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, without the authority of Her Majesty, or any of the Royal Family, or of any Government Department, assumes or uses in connexion with any trade, business, calling, or profession, the Royal arms, or arms so nearly resembling the same as to be calculated to deceive, in such a manner as to be calculated to lead other persons to believe that he is carrying on his trade, business, calling, or profession by or under such authority, shall be liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding twenty pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere use of the Royal arms is not an offence; the use must be calculated to lead persons to believe the user has royal/governmental authority. Separate provisions/summaries apply in Scotland and Ireland (see sects. 108, 117).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminalisation of false entries and false copies in registers
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person makes or causes to be made a false entry in any register kept under this Act, or a writing falsely purporting to be a copy of an entry in any such register, or produces or tenders in evidence any such writing knowing it to be false, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three specific offences are noted: making false register entries; making false copies purporting to be register copies; producing/tendering known false writings in evidence. Misdemeanors are punishable with fine and imprisonment at judge's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for patent infringement proceedings in Scotland
rubrics_metrics.description: In any action for infringement of a patent in Scotland the provisions of this Act with respect to calling in the aid of an assessor shall apply, and the action shall be tried without a jury, unless the Court shall otherwise direct; otherwise the Act does not affect jurisdiction and forms of process of Scottish Courts in such actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this section 'Court of Appeal' has a local meaning; actions in Scotland for infringement often take form of suspension and interdict or actions for damages. See local practice manuals referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary prosecution of offences in Scotland and Ireland
rubrics_metrics.description: Any offence under this Act declared to be punishable on summary conviction may be prosecuted in the Sheriff Court in Scotland and analogous procedures in Ireland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See specific sections for which offences are summary (sect. 105, 106) and for procedure references (sect. 108 for Scotland, sect. 117 for Ireland).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Act to Isle of Man with local modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: This Act shall extend to the Isle of Man, but nothing in this Act shall affect the jurisdiction of the Courts in the Isle of Man in proceedings for infringement or proceedings respecting a patent, design, or trade mark competent to those Courts; punishments for misdemeanors thereunder may differ (e.g., imprisonment up to two years with or without hard labour and fines up to £100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offences in the Isle of Man which would in England be punishable on summary conviction may be prosecuted and fines recovered at the instance of any person aggrieved in the manner for summary prosecutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification orders from Scottish/Ireland courts must be served on comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: If any rectification of a register under this Act is required in pursuance of any proceeding in a Court in Scotland or Ireland, a copy of the order, decree, or other authority for the rectification shall be served on the comptroller, and he shall rectify the register accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the registers' conformity across jurisdictions and requires administrative follow‑up by the comptroller on judicial orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act preserves jurisdiction of Scottish and Irish courts
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Act conferring special jurisdiction on the Court shall not, except so far as the jurisdiction extends, affect the jurisdiction of any Court in Scotland or Ireland in any proceedings relating to patents or to designs or to trade marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proceedings in Scotland the term 'the Court' means any Lord Ordinary of the Court of Session; for Ireland 'the Court' and 'Court of Appeal' have corresponding local definitions. The Act therefore coexists with local court systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal and transitional savings (continuation of former registers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain enactments are repealed by the Act but the repeal shall not affect the past operation of those enactments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text begins transitional provisions and savings for continuity of former registers and operations; full details continue beyond this chunk.
